design_rationale:
WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST. A member asks one question: what does it cost to be let out of the beans she cannot
deliver, and can it be done today. The records answer it with two obstacles she never mentions. The contract she is
talking about was never countersigned — her programme is one of the two the catalogue closes to withdrawal before
countersigning, so the application cannot simply be torn up — and its delivery window ran out on 25 February, a
fortnight before the call, so on the record as it stands there is no live window for a buyout to be given notice
against. A correct agent reads, in order: that the buyout charge is struck only after the window's last day falls
later than the day the contract is closed out and the committed bushels stand as the same written change leaves
them; that the bushels an amendment leaves the contract committing are settled only once the contract stands
countersigned with the committed bushels it was countersigned for on the record; and that the bushels countersigned
are not the bushels applied for but the marketing ceiling drawn from the grain business the equity ledger records.
Three writes follow in one order only, and the last of them is the member's own act. The customer volunteers none
of it: she says she sold more beans than she grew, that she will not drive in to the office, and — only if asked —
that her input account is behind.

DRAW (scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0003_farm_supply_and_grain_cooperative/tasks/grain_marketing_desk --task 1):
{"task": 1, "key": "farm_supply_and_grain_cooperative/grain_marketing_desk/1", "prerequisite_problems": 2,
"problems": 3, "factor_counts": [5, 4, 4]}. The tree carries two prerequisite problems and three computations, and
the drawn counts are taken as: grain_ext_contract_buyout_charge 5, grain_ext_countersigned_bushel_ceiling 4,
grain_ext_short_crop_amendment 4 — the multiset [5,4,4] as drawn.

ROUND 2 — WHAT THIS TASK'S REWORK CHANGED AND WHY. The round-1 audit
(env/env_0003_farm_supply_and_grain_cooperative/audits/policy_task/grain_marketing_desk/1.md) returned SOURCE-CHAIN RED
(F1-1) and SOURCE-TASK RED (F1-2), with observations F1-3 to F1-7.
  F1-1 / CG-A — the old `buyout <- amendment` edge waited on "the figures its registered amendments leave", a state
  a contract with no registered amendment satisfies vacuously. The edge now waits on a state the records plainly
  falsify: the last day of the delivery window must fall later than the day the contract is closed out. At
  frozen_time that day is 25 February 2026 against a call on 12 March 2026 — false by fifteen days, on the face of
  grain_contracts.delivery_end_date, and nothing about the emptiness of a quantifier is doing the work.
  F1-6 — the old amendment extended the delivery window of a member who had just said she could not deliver, and
  its only effect on the charge was to make her own notice cheaper. The amendment now does what base's own sentence
  contemplates for a short crop ("A live contract may be amended in writing to change the bushels committed"): it
  cuts the contract to the bushels the tickets credit plus the share of the shortfall the cooperative has already
  sold on and will not release, and it carries the window forward at the same time so that the contract can be
  closed out at all rather than left to run into default — which base says is the dearer of the two outcomes for
  the member. The notice window is honoured rather than priced: the buyout is put through fifteen days before the
  revised close, against the programme's seven-day notice window.
  F1-2 / CG-17 — grain_pricing_intake.order_type has no value that records a signed buyout instruction, so the base
  gate signed_buyout_instruction could be evidenced only by reading a target offer as a buyout paper. The blueprint
  is frozen, so the departure is declared where it belongs, in this policy's own `overwrite`: the base clause is
  superseded by "A contract is closed out only by the member's own hand: the member puts the buyout through
  themselves, and no instruction the member has lodged with the grain desk for another purpose stands as authority
  to close a contract out." The buyout tool no longer takes a pricing_order_id, the world seeds no instruction at
  all, and the one record that used to be both the authority and the market level is gone.
  F1-3 — with the notice requirement inherited unchanged and satisfied at fifteen days, and the notice multiplier
  removed from the computation, the arrival-time reading and the handling-time reading now agree.
  F1-4 — the seven tickets stand against an application that was never countersigned. The countersigning policy's
  rule now says so in terms ("whose tickets stand held against the contract until it is countersigned and whose
  bushels come off the contract only as loads are applied to it"), which is exactly the state base's
  contract_live_for_application describes, and the seed keeps the contract's bushels still owed untouched.
  F1-5 — the notice factor, whose fall-through charged every buyout the late-notice penalty, is gone; and the
  replacement level, which the old fall-through manufactured out of the contract's own basis, is gone with it. The
  charge is now struck on rates the catalogue publishes: the floor premium the member paid, the default penalty,
  the loss multiplier and the flat administrative fee.
  F1-7 — CG-3 (the rule/compute tier mismatch on forward_reserve_bu) is fixed in compute, which now tests that the
  window has not opened before it reaches the near-window tier. CG-10 (marketed_units_* summing every ledger event
  type) is fixed by filtering on patronage_units_accrued, and the rule says so. CG-12 is fixed by moving the
  recent-history tier to a twenty-four month window divided by two and by lifting the ceiling percentages to 88 and
  78 and the part-delivered buyout fee to 140.00, none of which equals a tier parameter on any programme of the
  catalogue. CG-13's inert fall-through belonged to the old off-facility allowance factor, which no longer exists:
  the allowance is a constant of the amendment rule and the ladder that replaced it decides the retained share,
  whose fall-through (retain the whole shortfall) is the live case for a member with no tickets. CG-14 stands as an
  observation and is answered below.
  CG-8, which the audit demonstrated against task 0, is answered here: the amendment no longer restates the bushels
  still owed at all — it restates the bushels the contract commits, and its rule says outright that "An amendment
  does not touch the bushels still owed on the contract: those follow the loads applied to it and are not restated
  here." Exactly one write of this difficulty now brings about the state task 0's roll sentence waits on.
  CG-14 — grain_amendment's amendment fee is inherited in full and is not discharged by any write of this
  difficulty, because grain_ledger.deduction_type admits no amendment-fee class and no tool may invent one. The fee
  is not overridden, not waived and not quietly dropped from the charter; it simply has no line to stand on in this
  schema, and no scored parameter of this task turns on it.

SCOPE. Task 0 occupies the delivery-balance, delayed-price carry, roll-charge and settlement-payment ground with
record_contract_delivery_balance_c52b7782, book_delayed_price_carry_charge_ebb3e3fc,
execute_futures_month_roll_2054762f and release_grain_settlement_payment_379b8a52. This task claims the entry and
exit of a contract: grain_ext_countersigned_bushel_ceiling, grain_ext_short_crop_amendment and
grain_ext_contract_buyout_charge, with countersign_grain_contract_d95afc7d, register_contract_amendment_850dd44e
and execute_contract_buyout_11de6ced. The two scopes share no policy, no tool and no base subject, and together the
two tasks cover every extended policy of the difficulty.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
  root problem: grain_ext_contract_buyout_charge (the customer's surface request: what it costs to be let out of
  the balance, done today).
  prerequisite problems: grain_ext_short_crop_amendment, grain_ext_countersigned_bushel_ceiling.
  edge 1  grain_ext_contract_buyout_charge <- grain_ext_short_crop_amendment
    kind value_input; gate = the compute binding undelivered_bu; form state.
    prerequisite sentence: "The buyout charge is struck only after the last day of the contract's delivery window
    falls later than the day the contract is closed out, with the bushels the contract commits standing as the same
    written change leaves them."
    four-point test: (1) the ordering connective is "only after"; (2) what it waits on is a record-visible state —
    two fields of the contract record, its last day of delivery against today and its committed bushels; (3) no
    tool name, policy id or code token; (4) it is a hard requirement over exactly those two figures. Exactly one
    write of this difficulty sets delivery_end_date and the committed bushels together:
    register_contract_amendment_850dd44e. Derivation: the sentence says the window's last day must fall later than
    the day of the buyout; the contract read at action 2 shows 25 February 2026 against a call on 12 March; the
    amendment policy's own rule says an amendment moves that last day out by the programme's extension allowance
    and restates the bushels committed at the same time; so the resolving action is the write that registers it.
    handling-time state (condition): the window's last day falls later than the day of the buyout and the committed
    bushels are the figure the written change leaves. False at the opening: delivery_end_date = 2026-02-25,
    amendment_count = 0, contracted_bushels = 26000. Once resolved: 2026-03-27, 1 and 15137.0.
  edge 2  grain_ext_short_crop_amendment <- grain_ext_countersigned_bushel_ceiling
    kind value_input; gate = the compute binding committed_bu; form state.
    prerequisite sentence: "The bushels an amendment leaves the contract committing are settled only once the
    contract stands countersigned and binding on both sides, with the committed bushels it was countersigned for
    standing on the record."
    four-point test: (1) "only once"; (2) a record-visible state — the contract's standing and its committed
    bushels; (3) no tool, policy id or code token; (4) exactly the state the condition names. Exactly one write of
    this difficulty moves a contract out of applied standing and stamps the bushels it binds:
    countersign_grain_contract_d95afc7d. Derivation: the contract read at action 2 stands in applied standing with
    an empty activation date; the countersigning policy's rule says what bushels a contract is countersigned for;
    the resolving action follows.
    handling-time state (condition): the contract stands active or delivering with its committed bushels at the
    countersigned figure. False at the opening: status = applied, activated_date empty. Once resolved: active,
    12 March 2026, 19834.0.
  topological order: grain_ext_countersigned_bushel_ceiling, grain_ext_short_crop_amendment,
  grain_ext_contract_buyout_charge, at actions 8, 10 and 12.
  parallel edges: none — the tree is a chain and each edge's own sentence fixes the order.
  per-edge deletion sensitivity (executed): skipping the amendment leaves the buyout charge at 1456.47 instead of
  830.56; skipping the countersigning leaves the amendment's revised commitment at 21102.0 instead of 15137.0.
  the customer never mentions a prerequisite: proved in prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint.
  the tool layer blocks nothing: proved in prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
  Write at action 8 (subject grain_contract_activated): the only base policy governing that subject is
  grain_lifecycle_progression, which declares no structured eligibility, so it is inherited as policy scope — the
  desk countersigns an application once the programme's paperwork is on file, and the contract record carries both
  the signed marketing agreement and the completed credit review, which this programme requires. No time gate.
  Write at action 10 (subject grain_contract_amended): governed by grain_agg_open_position_cap, whose gate
  amendment_live_contract measures an amendment that raises bushels against the cap while the contract stands in
  active or delivering — this amendment lowers them, which the same sentence says is never blocked by the cap — and
  by grain_amendment, whose gate amendment_live_only requires active or delivering standing and whose time gate
  amendment_within_window requires registration no later than the amendment window running from the activation
  date, counted in whole calendar days with that date counting as day zero and the final day still in time. The
  contract is countersigned on 12 March 2026 and the amendment registered the same day, day zero of a ten-day
  window; the boundary cases are recorded in temporal_feasibility. The amendment lowers the committed bushels to
  15,137, which is above the 12,077.71 net bushels already delivered, so base's refusal to lower bushels below what
  has been delivered is respected, and the window moves to 27 March 2026, exactly the thirty-day extension
  allowance and so an amendment rather than a roll.
  Write at action 12 (subject grain_contract_cancelled): governed by grain_buyout. Its authorisation gate
  signed_buyout_instruction is superseded clause by clause in this policy's `overwrite` and so is not inherited;
  what remains of grain_buyout is inherited in full and carried as policy scope, including the notice sentence —
  the buyout is put through on 12 March 2026 against a window closing 27 March, fifteen days of notice against the
  programme's seven-day window — and the sentence that the charge is drawn on the next settlement statement or
  invoiced to the crop input account, which is why a collection charge arises where no statement stands.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. The narrowest object is contract GC-118476 (soybeans, crop year 2026, Minimum Price
Contract). The correlation key is contract_number for every write. Rows entering each aggregate: the seven
grain_delivery_applied tickets (credited bushels, hauled-load credit, hold period, loss multiplier, administrative
fee), the equity ledger's three accrual rows (the marketing average, the ceiling percentage and the patron release
factor) and the crop input account (the collection charge). Rows deliberately excluded: none of the equity ledger's
rows is an allocation or a retain, so the marketed-bushel aggregates count each year's bushels once; and no
settlement statement stands on this contract, which is why a collection charge arises at all.

WORLD, ROW BY ROW, AND WHAT WOULD CHANGE WITHOUT IT. The seven tickets carry the reconciliation: remove the two Ash
Grove tickets and the off-facility allowance stops biting; remove the late-posted ticket of 6 February and the hold
period runs from the delivery date instead, taking the hold shrink from the short rate to the long one; remove four
of them and the hauled-load credit falls to the low rate and the retained share to the part-crop figure. The
contract's applied standing is what makes the countersigning necessary, its closed window is what makes the
amendment necessary, and its 26,000 applied-for bushels are what the ceiling bites on. The equity membership and
its three accrual rows are the member's marketing history: without the 2025 row there is no grain business inside
twelve months, the marketing average falls to the four-year divisor and the patron release factor falls to one. The
crop input account's past-due standing lifts the collection charge from the standard figure to the arrears figure.
  Near-misses planted on purpose: the accrual of 31 August 2023 sits thirty months back — inside the thirty-six
  month window the fall-through method reads and outside the twenty-four month window the applicable tier reads, so
  a careless reader who uses one window for both figures lands on a different average; and the ticket of 6 February
  was posted thirteen days after it was received, so a reader who anchors the hold on the delivery date reaches
  thirty-four days and the long hold rate where the rule's own sentence sends them to twenty-one days and the short
  one.
  Automatic clauses checked: the contract stands in applied standing, so no load has been applied to it, nothing
  stands in the unpriced position and no carry arises; no settlement statement stands, so no checkoff, retain or
  payment is owed; a contract in applied standing cannot default, because default is a transition out of active or
  delivering, which is why a window that has run out leaves the application in limbo rather than in default; the
  programme closes withdrawal before countersigning, so tearing the application up is not available. No cache field
  is used as a difficulty.

PERSONA. Marta Berg is quick, practical and slightly embarrassed to be making the call. She opens with the whole
request — she sold more beans forward than the farm grew, she cannot haul the rest, she wants to know what it costs
to be let out of the balance on that bean contract and to have it dealt with today — and adds that she is not
driving in to the office. Her identity details come out one at a time and only on request. She knows the shape of
the contract and not its detail, tells the agent to go by the tickets, and admits her input account is behind only
when asked. Her two conditional behaviours are in the narration: if she is told some part of the paperwork has to
be put in order first she says to do whatever needs doing and waits, and when the buyout is handed to her she puts
it through and reads back what comes up. She closes on being told the contract is closed out and what the charge
came to.

REACHABILITY IN ONE CONVERSATION. Every read is a share tool call against records already in the world; the three
writes are synchronous at one frozen_time. The countersigning is a desk act on paperwork already on file; the
amendment is a written change the desk registers on the spot; the buyout is the member's own act, handed over by
the agent and run by her inside the same call. Nothing waits on a delivery, a clearing, a review, a board or a
future date. Questions a real agent would ask and the persona answers: who is calling, proof of identity, where the
loads went, what the beans are worth (she does not know and says so), whether she will come in to sign (she will
not), and whether the input account is current (it is not).

DIFFICULTY, AND THE EASY MISTAKES. Buying out on the record as it stands gives 21,550-odd rather than 830.56, and
buying out after the countersigning but with no amendment gives 1456.47. Countersigning for the 26,000 applied for
rather than the ceiling leaves the amendment restating 21,102 bushels. Reading the thirty-six month window where
the applicable tier reads twenty-four inflates the marketing average by a third. Anchoring the hold on the delivery
date rather than the posting date takes the hold shrink from 0.40 to 0.75 per cent. Reading only the computation
documents gives 6,525 bushels countersigned, a commitment of 19,834 and a charge of 964.75.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate and verify the member; read the contract, the tickets, the equity membership and ledger
and the crop input account. Countersign GC-118476 for 19,834 bushels. Register the amendment moving the delivery
window to 27 March 2026, the first amendment on the contract, restating the commitment at 15,137 bushels. Hand the
buyout to the member, who puts it through at 830.56.

VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN. The three computes were evaluated at their own handling times (initial_state plus every
earlier gold write) with the skill's evaluator, giving 19834.0, 15137.0 and 830.56, equal to the gold arguments and
to computations[].expected. Substituting every factor's baseline at once gives 6525.0, 19834.0 and 964.75, each
different from gold. Per factor the baseline substitution moves the result; the thirteen figures are recorded in
computations[].factor_sensitivity. The prerequisite sensitivity run gives 1456.47 (skip the amendment) and 21102.0
(skip the countersigning).

FORWARD AND REVERSE SWEEP. Forward: every binding that reads the world or chooses quotes its rule sentence in
compute_basis. Reverse: each rule was read through for promises — the marketing average basis, the ceiling
percentage, the hauled-load credit, the forward reserve, the ticket credit selection, the off-facility allowance,
the retained share, the hold shrink, the hold anchor, the release rate, the loss multiplier, the patron release
factor, the administrative fee and the collection charge — and each is implemented by the binding named. The
roundings promised ("struck in whole bushels", "rounded to the cent once") are implemented by RND(...,0) and one
RND(...,2); the interval conventions ("over the last thirty-six months", "the last twenty-four months", "inside the
last twelve months", "counted in calendar days up to the day the amendment is registered") by within_months=36, 24
and 12 and by DAYS from the anchor; the floor that bushels already in the pit cannot be cut away by MX against the
net bushels the tickets carry.

OVERRIDES DECLARED. grain_ext_countersigned_bushel_ceiling supersedes two clauses of grain_agg_open_position_cap:
the clause that writes a contract only where the open position plus the bushels committed stay under the ceiling,
and the clause defining the open forward position and the production history average. grain_ext_short_crop_amendment
declares none: it refines the amendment's arithmetic without contradicting any sentence of grain_amendment.
grain_ext_contract_buyout_charge supersedes two clauses of grain_buyout: the authorisation clause, replaced by the
member's own act, and the buyout price clause, replaced by the release-rate arithmetic. Every other base sentence,
eligibility, constant and terminal state is inherited untouched.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. With the extended yaml, compute, expected, gold and this dossier
masked, working only from the policy prose that will be published, the tool schemas, the records the share tools
return and the member's own words: she asks what it costs to be let out; the buyout paragraph waits on the window's
last day falling later than the day of the buyout and on the committed bushels standing as the written change
leaves them, and the contract contradicts both; the amendment paragraph waits on the contract standing
countersigned with its committed bushels on the record, which the applied standing contradicts; the countersigning
paragraph strikes the bushels bound from the marketing ceiling. That fixes the order — countersign, amend, buy out
— and the ladders and records give 19,834, 15,137 and 830.56. The draft agrees with gold, and no second reading of
the prose produced a different order or figure.

SOLVABILITY EVIDENCE AGAINST GOLD. The countersigning carries its governing policy as policy scope with the
contract's paperwork fields cited; the amendment carries all three gates with the contract's standing, number,
committed bushels, activation date and amendment count cited, the activation date established by the preceding
write, and a temporal entry whose basis is copied from the base eligibility; the buyout carries grain_buyout as
policy scope, its authorisation gate having been superseded clause by clause. Every required customer input occurs
verbatim in user_scenario, and every seeded contract and ledger row carries a seed_consistency entry naming the
base policy that governs it.

MANUAL VALUES GATES RUN AFTER THE SCRIPTS PASSED (task 1, round 2).
  Length, breadth and the hidden test: walked from the surface goal to each figure — what the buyout costs -> the
  window's last day and the committed bushels must stand as the written change leaves them -> the contract must
  stand countersigned with its committed bushels on the record. Removing either edge changes a scored figure
  (1456.47 / 21102.0). The root problem is the member's own act, handed over and run on the spot.
  Expression of the need and the simulator's boundary: the member states the object, the timing, that she will not
  come in to sign and that she will put through what is handed to her. She never reads policy and supplies no
  figure.
  Chronology of the opening world: every fact she volunteers points at seeded rows; she foresees no charge.
  Base eligibility and the time anchor: checked per subject, with the amendment window's boundary cases recorded
  and the buyout's notice sentence satisfied at fifteen days against a seven-day window.
  Authoritative facts and the business object: the contract record is the only authority for the standing, the
  window and the committed bushels; the member's own execution is the authority for the cancellation, declared in
  `overwrite`.
  Prerequisite sentences: the four-point test was applied to both; the state form was available and used in each;
  neither rule says anything else about its dependency; each state is brought about by exactly one write of this
  difficulty.
  Two-way equivalence of rule and compute: every ladder is stated tier by tier in the rule, the tiers are pairwise
  disjoint as stated, and no two tiers of any ladder select the same value or method on any programme of the
  catalogue.
  Factors bear weight and the labels are honest: each factor's baseline is what its baseline paragraph states; the
  method factors change a window, an anchor, a selection rule or the rate a release is struck at; the parameter
  factors select values.
  Draft recomputation from the visible context: performed and recorded above; it agrees with gold.

ROUND 3 — WHAT THE RENDER-LAYER AUDIT SENT BACK TO THE SOURCE, AND WHAT CHANGED HERE. This task passed the blind
runtime audit on every item, including both hops and all three scored figures. The changes below are the
charter-wide settlements the same audit asked for, applied to this task's three policies.
  P1 — "struck in whole bushels" had no rounding mode. The audit showed it biting here: the restated commitment
  comes to 15,136.552 before the striking, and the reader had to guess between 15,136 and 15,137, which moves the
  buyout charge between 830.40 and 830.56. The ceiling and amendment rules now read "struck in whole bushels, a part bushel taken
  to the nearest whole bushel and a half bushel taken upward" — the buyout's own striking sentence was not
  reached until round 4 below — and all three computes moved from RND(x, 0) to
  int(x + 0.5) so that prose and machine agree at the half bushel too. The scored figures are unchanged:
  19,834.0 countersigned, 15,137.0 committed and 830.56 charged.
  P5 — "applied to the contract" with two extensions. The ceiling's hauled-load credit, the amendment's ticket
  credit and the buyout's loss multiplier all count every load standing against the contract and now say so
  ("whatever the disposition"); the buyout's administrative fee counts only "loads the member directed to the
  contract at the scale" and now says that. One binding moved with the words: the release rate's second tier
  counted only the loads directed to the contract while its sentence spoke of every ticket standing against it, and
  the binding is now the broad count. No figure moves — this contract carries no load run straight through, and the
  release rate is settled on its first tier by the programme's floor premium.
  P4 — an in-force clause whose defining sentence was retired. `grain_buyout`'s clause "Where the market has fallen
  the loss is zero and only the administrative fee is charged; the cooperative does not pay the member the
  difference" spoke of a market loss that this policy's own overwrite had already retired. It is now the third
  declared retirement on `grain_buyout`, replaced by the sentence that carries the same protection in the terms
  this charter does use: "Where the release rate, the loss multiplier and the patron release factor between them
  come to nothing, the bushels carry nothing and only the administrative fee and the collection charge are charged;
  the cooperative does not pay the member the difference." That sentence is in the baseline paragraph, so the
  computation document carries it, and it is exactly what the compute's floor around the bushel term does.
  P6 — catalogue charges no write books. The Minimum Price Contract's setup fee of 85.00, its amendment fee of
  75.00 and its extension charge of 0.0200 a bushel are all normative and none can be booked: grain_ledger's ten
  deduction classes contain no setup fee, amendment fee or extension charge, and grain_contracts carries no money
  field. The blueprint is frozen and no tool may invent a class, so all three clauses are inherited in full,
  neither overridden nor waived, and no scored figure turns on them. This is the same judgement recorded for the
  amendment fee in round 2, now stated for all three on the same footing.
  Recomputation after every change: 19,834.0, 15,137.0 and 830.56, equal to the gold arguments; whole-baseline
  fall-backs 6,525.0, 19,834.0 and 964.75; all thirteen factor sensitivities unchanged.

ROUND 4 — THE TIGHTENING BEFORE THE RE-RENDER. The round-3 source audit passed this task on all four relationships
and recorded five observations under its stricter test. Three bear on this task and all are now closed. No scored
figure moved: 19,834.0, 15,137.0 and 830.56 stand, as do all thirteen factor sensitivities and the three
whole-baseline fall-backs.
  R3-1 — the buyout policy struck its undelivered bushels in whole bushels and stated no rounding mode anywhere in
  the policy, so unlike the ceiling there was nothing for a reader to carry across from another sentence. Its
  striking sentence now reads "…struck in whole bushels, a part bushel taken to the nearest whole bushel and a half
  bushel taken upward, and never below zero", matching its compute's int(x + 0.5). On this world 15,137 − 12,077.71
  = 3,059.29, which is not a half bushel, so the undelivered bushels stay 3,059 and the charge stays 830.56. The
  ceiling's second striking sentence was tagged in the same pass.
  R3-2 — this dossier's sentence "All three rules now read 'struck in whole bushels, a part bushel…'" was false of
  the buyout when it was written. It is restated above to name the two policies it was true of and to point at the
  round-4 change that makes the third true, and every other completeness claim in this dossier was re-read against
  the artifacts in the same pass.
  R3-5 — the amendment's disclaimer was the last normative sentence using the bare phrase. It now reads "An
  amendment does not touch the bushels still owed on the contract: those follow the loads the member directed to
  the contract at the scale and are not restated here", which is the narrow phrase this charter uses and the right
  one for a balance that falls as loads are applied. It governs no binding, so nothing moves.
  R3-3 and R3-4 fall in task 0's policies and are recorded in that dossier; neither touches this task's figures.
user_scenario:
Marta Berg took over the row-crop ground at Berg Hollow Farms in Hancock County when her father stepped back, and she talks about it the way somebody does who is still doing two jobs at once: quickly, with the combine yield map open on the laptop beside her. The beans went in late on the west quarters and came off light, and she has been putting off this telephone call for a fortnight. She makes the reason for it plain almost at once, and she is careful to say what she wants rather than ask for sympathy: she sold more beans forward than the farm grew, she cannot haul the rest of them, and she wants to know what it costs to be let out of the balance on that bean contract and to have it dealt with today rather than left hanging. She says she is not driving in to the office over it, and that whatever has to be signed had better be something she can do from the kitchen table.
She gives her name and the farm at the start. Pressed for something to pull the account up with, she reads out the membership number from the top of last year's patronage notice, M-11487. If she is asked to prove she is who she says she is she offers the mobile first, 5150117306, and then the last four of the taxpayer number, 1163, and she gives them one at a time rather than all at once.
Asked about the contract, she knows the shape of it and not the detail: beans, this crop year, hauled to Bergen Siding apart from two loads that went to Ash Grove because the scale at Bergen was down that week. She is fairly sure she hauled seven loads in total but says to go by the tickets rather than her memory. If she is asked what the beans were worth, or what it would cost the elevator to replace them, she says that is the desk's side of it and she has no idea. If she is asked whether her input account is current she goes quiet for a second and says no, it is behind, she knows, and the seed bill is part of why she needs to know the figure today.
She does not ask the agent to do anything in particular beyond getting her out of the balance, and if she is told that some part of the paperwork on the contract has to be put in order first she says that is fine, do whatever needs doing, and she waits without pressing. When the buyout is handed over for her to put through herself, she puts it through and reads back what comes up on her screen exactly as it appears. She will not put anything through that has not been handed to her, and she does not ask for it.
Once she hears that the contract has been closed out and what the charge came to, she writes the figure down, says she will settle it with the rest of the account and that she would rather not be in this position again next year, and rings off. If she is instead told that the contract cannot be closed out today, she asks once what the obstacle is, takes the answer as given, and leaves it there.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Pull up the membership profile the caller names so the account the call concerns is identified.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Without the member's internal reference nothing else on the account can be read or written.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Check the two details the caller states against the profile and record the outcome.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Identity must clear before any grain business is read out or transacted on the account.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the member's grain marketing contract: its programme, standing, committed bushels, price terms, delivery point and window.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The standing shows the application was never countersigned, the window shows it has already run out, and the committed bushels and price terms are inputs to all three computations.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read every ticket standing against the contract with its facility, condition, net bushels and the day it was posted.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The tickets give the bushels credited and the hauled-load credit, the facilities give the off-facility allowance, the posting dates give the hold period, and the loads decide the loss multiplier and the administrative fee.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the member's equity account: its class, standing and voting position.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The equity standing and voting position decide the marketing average, the ceiling percentage and the patron release factor.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the grain bushels the equity ledger records the member marketing in each of the last three fiscal years.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Those bushels are the member's marketing history, from which the marketing average, the ceiling percentage and the patron release factor are drawn.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the member's crop input account and its standing.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The standing of that account decides the collection charge carried on the buyout where there is no settlement to draw it from.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock countersign_grain_contract_d95afc7d so the write it performs can be called.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first half of the unlock/call pair; it changes no record and is done once for this tool.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Countersign the member's application for GC-118476 for the bushels the marketing ceiling allows.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: grain_ext_countersigned_bushel_ceiling is the only policy that computes the bushels a contract is countersigned for, and this tool is the write that binds them.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.contract_id: The value is the internal reference of contract GC-118476, the member's only grain marketing contract, returned by the grain contract lookup at action 2. The tool's schema line reads 'Id class — the internal reference of the grain marketing contract application being countersigned; it identifies one contract record and is reachable from the grain contract lookup for the member before this call.' It is unique because one contract stands for this member and it is the bean contract the caller is asking about.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.countersigned_bushels: The value is 19834.0. The member applied for 26,000 bushels. The equity ledger records marketed grain business of 22,400 bushels in fiscal 2023, 19,800 in 2024 and 21,300 in 2025 — 63,500 over thirty-six months, 41,100 over twenty-four and 21,300 inside twelve — and the equity account stands active, so the marketing average is the twenty-four month total divided by the recent history window of two, 20,550 bushels. The thirty-six month total of 63,500 is above the established marketer threshold of 55,000 and the account carries voting rights, so the ceiling percentage is 88, giving a ceiling of 18,084 bushels. Seven tickets stand against the contract, whatever the disposition, carrying 12,077.71 bushels, above the programme's smallest contract of 5,000, so the hauled-load credit is 250 bushels for each of the seven, 1,750. The delivery window opened on 27 December 2025 and loads stand against the contract, so no forward reserve is held back. The ceiling with the credit is 19,834, which is less than the 26,000 applied for, so the contract is countersigned for 19834.0.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock register_contract_amendment_850dd44e so the write it performs can be called.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first half of the unlock/call pair; it changes no record and is done once for this tool.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Register the written amendment that moves the last day of the delivery window out by the programme's extension allowance and restates the bushels the contract commits.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: grain_ext_short_crop_amendment computes the bushels an amendment leaves the contract committing, and this tool is the write that registers it.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.contract_id: The value is the internal reference of contract GC-118476 returned by the grain contract lookup at action 2, cited by the tool's schema line 'Id class — the internal reference of the grain marketing contract the amendment is registered against'. It is unique because the member holds one grain contract.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.contract_number: The value is GC-118476. The basis is the contract record returned at action 2, whose contract_number field reads GC-118476, and the tool's schema line 'Id class — the contract number the member quotes when hauling or pricing, which identifies the same marketing contract on paper'. It is unique because one contract stands for this member.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.revised_delivery_end_date: The value is 2026-03-27. The basis is the rule sentence 'it moves the last day of the delivery window out by the full extension allowance the member's marketing programme carries, counted in calendar days from the last day the contract currently calls for', together with the catalogue entry for the Minimum Price Contract, whose delivery extension allowance is 30 calendar days. The contract currently calls for 25 February 2026, and 30 calendar days after it is 27 March 2026. It is unique because the allowance is fixed by the programme and the starting day is the last day standing on the contract record; moving it further would not be an amendment at all but a roll.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.amendment_count: The value is 1. The basis is the contract record returned at action 2, whose amendment_count field reads 0, and the base rule of grain_amendment, 'A contract may take no more amendments than the programme's ceiling, and each one carries the programme's amendment fee, charged whether or not the amendment later proves unnecessary.' This is the first amendment registered against the contract, so the running count once it is registered is 1, which is also the ceiling the Minimum Price Contract allows.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.revised_contracted_bushels: The value is 15137.0. The contract is countersigned for 19,834 bushels. Seven tickets stand against it: five received at Bergen Siding Elevator, the facility the contract calls for, carrying 8,800.63 net bushels, and two received at Ash Grove Annex carrying 3,277.08. Because tickets stand that were received at another facility, the home tickets are credited at their net bushels and the others at their net bushels less the off-facility allowance of 0.75 per cent, giving 3,252.50 and a credited total of 12,053.13. The ledger shows the last ticket received on 6 February 2026 and posted on 19 February 2026, so the hold runs from the posting day and is 21 days; that is longer than the short hold period of 14 days but not the long period of 28, so the hold shrink is 0.40 per cent, leaving 12,004.92 credited. The shortfall is 19,834 less 12,004.92, that is 7,829.08 bushels. The tickets credit more than half the bushels the contract commits and seven of them stand, so the retained share is the short-crop retention of 0.40, retaining 3,131.63 bushels. 12,004.92 plus 3,131.63, struck in whole bushels, is 15137.0, which is above the 12,077.71 net bushels the tickets carry and so is not floored.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock execute_contract_buyout_11de6ced so the write it performs can be called.

evaluation_criteria.necessity: grain_ext_contract_buyout_charge computes the charge the buyout carries; closing a contract out is the member's own act, so it is handed over and called by them.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.contract_id: The value is the internal reference of contract GC-118476 returned by the grain contract lookup at action 2, cited by the tool's schema line 'Id class — the internal reference of the grain marketing contract being bought out'. It is unique because one contract stands for this member.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.customer_id: The value is the member's internal reference returned by the membership profile lookup at action 0, cited by the tool's schema line 'Id class — the internal reference of the member buying the contract out'. It is unique because one member matches the membership number M-11487 the caller states.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.buyout_charge_usd: The value is 830.56. The contract commits 15,137 bushels once the amendment is registered and the tickets standing against it carry 12,077.71 net bushels, so the undelivered bushels are 3,059. The Minimum Price Contract carries a price floor premium of 0.2400 a bushel, so the release is struck at that rate. The member has delivered 12,077.71 bushels against 15,137 committed, more than half, across seven loads, so the loss multiplier is 0.75. The equity account carries voting rights and the equity ledger records 21,300 bushels of grain business inside the last twelve months, so the patron release factor is 0.90. The contract carries a registered amendment and loads stand applied to it, so the administrative fee is 275.00. No settlement statement stands on the contract and the member's crop input account stands past due, so the collection charge is 60.00. 3,059 x 0.2400 x 0.75 x 0.90 = 495.56, and with 275.00 and 60.00 added the charge is 830.56.

edges.condition: The last day of the contract's delivery window falls later than the day of the buyout, and the bushels the contract commits are the figure the written change leaves.
edges.policy_source: The buyout charge is struck only after the last day of the contract's delivery window falls later than the day the contract is closed out, with the bushels the contract commits standing as the same written change leaves them.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The contract's delivery window ran out on 25 February 2026, fifteen days before frozen_time, so its last day falls earlier and not later than the day the contract would be closed out; and the bushels it commits are the 26,000 the member applied for, which no written change has touched, its amendment count standing at nil.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Registering the amendment writes a last day of 2026-03-27, which falls later than the day of the buyout, an amendment count of 1 and committed bushels of 15137.0, so the undelivered bushels and the administrative fee both take the figures the change leaves.

edges.condition: The contract stands in active or delivering standing and its committed bushels are the figure it was countersigned for.
edges.policy_source: The bushels an amendment leaves the contract committing are settled only once the contract stands countersigned and binding on both sides, with the committed bushels it was countersigned for standing on the record.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The contract stands in applied standing with an empty activation date: it was applied for on 18 November 2025 and never countersigned, so the committed bushels on the record are the 26,000 the member asked for rather than a figure the cooperative has bound itself to.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Countersigning writes status active, an activation date of 2026-03-12 and committed bushels of 19834.0, so the shortfall the amendment works on is struck against the countersigned figure.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain, so no two writes are free to be reordered: the amendment's own rule waits on the contract standing countersigned with its committed bushels on the record, and the buyout's own rule waits on the window's last day falling later than the day of the buyout and on the committed bushels standing as the written change leaves them. Each order is fixed by a prerequisite sentence rather than by convention, and there are no parallel edges to prove commutative.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the amendment leaves the buyout charge at 1456.47 instead of 830.56: the contract still commits 19,834 bushels so the undelivered bushels are 7,756 rather than 3,059, and with no amendment on the record the administrative fee falls from the amended-contract fee of 275.00 to the part-delivered fee of 140.00.

Skipping the countersigning leaves the amendment's revised commitment at 21102.0 instead of 15137.0: the committed bushels stay at the 26,000 applied for, so the shortfall rises to 13,995.08 and the tickets no longer credit half the bushels committed, which takes the retained share from the short-crop retention of 0.40 to the part-crop retention of 0.65.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only what it costs to be let out of the balance on the bean contract and that it be dealt with today. It never mentions countersigning, an application standing unsigned, an amendment, a delivery window, a bushel ceiling or a retained share, and it drops no hint that anything must be put in order first. The member's one line about paperwork is a reaction, given only after the agent has said something must be put in order, and she asks no question about what it is.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: No function in task_tools.py validates a prerequisite. countersign_grain_contract_d95afc7d calls ctx.update with the figure given; register_contract_amendment_850dd44e calls ctx.update with the date, count and commitment given; execute_contract_buyout_11de6ced mints a row id, calls ctx.create for the charge and ctx.update to close the contract out. None reads another row, tests a standing, counts a ticket or returns a refusal, so an agent that buys the contract out first still gets a normal receipt and a terminal hash that differs from gold.
